practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran starter profile (8th NFL season, 94% snap share) — elevated Questionable active conversion (84%) & Wednesday maintenance tolerance.
factors: Did Not Participate (DNP) on Wednesday; remains sidelined from practice
practiceReport.beatComment: Risner did not play in the Bengals' loss to the Commanders on Monday night due to multiple knee injuries. The starting right guard remains day-to-day with the issue, meaning he could return for Sunday's game against the Saints. If Risner cannot suit up for Week 12, Jalen Rivers is set to start at right guard again.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Cashius Howell
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Howell suffered a right wrist injury during Sunday's overtime win against the Titans, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result. The defensive lineman has already undergone surgery, per Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com, and in Howell's absence, Shemar Stewart will stand to see an increase in workload at defensive end.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Oren Burks
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Burks has been working through a groin issue for the past couple of weeks, and he aggravated the injury during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. His placement on IR means he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 20.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Ja'Sir Taylor
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Taylor signed a one-year contract with the Bengals in early April. The cornerback is set to play a key reserve role in the team's secondary once he can return to the field. Taylor will need to miss at least the first four games of the regular season on IR before becoming eligible to return to the Bengals' active roster.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Erick All Jr.
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: All, who sustained the injury in Sunday's win over the Ravens, has now torn the ACL in his right knee three times during his career. He first tore the ACL during his final collegiate season at Iowa in 2023, then had his 2024 rookie campaign with the Bengals cut short after damaging the ligament again. Given the timing of the injury along with the fact that he'll be working his way back from a third surgery of the same knee, All is far from guaranteed to be ready to play when the 2027 season gets underway.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Tanner Hudson
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Hudson suffered a torn pectoral muscle during the team's 31-24 win over Miami in Week 5, so his transition to IR comes as no surprise. In his absence, Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample and Erick All will continue to operate as the team's primary options at tight end.
